# nonLength

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** a valid array-like length.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonLength() — Checks whether a value is **not** a valid array-like length. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonLength(value: unknown): boolean;
```

`nonLength(value)` is the same test as `!isLength(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

A whole number from `0` up to `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` — the range a `length` property may hold.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not a valid array-like length; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonLength(-1); // => true
nonLength(1.5); // => true
nonLength("3"); // => true
nonLength(0); // => false
nonLength(42); // => false
nonLength(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); // => false
```
